belay.1: Gear belay below a faint white dyke in the slab, reached by traversing right along a grassy ledge.
belay.2: Fixed anchor on the skyline, reached by going right from the thin ledge and up a short gully.
belay.3: Gear belay on a heather ledge above the arete with the fixed pins.
belay.5: Fixed anchor on the skyline, about 50 ft right of the second bolt along the traverse.

belay.1: Chain anchor on Madsen's Ledge, at the top of the pitch.
belay.4: Hanging belay at the top of the left-leaning crack system.
belay.5: Hanging belay just past the last hard section, up and right of the big flake.
belay.6: Double-ring anchor on a large ledge at the end of the pitch.
belay.7: With a 60 m rope, stop at the far-left anchor with oversized chain links; otherwise go on to the three-bolt anchor.

belay.1: Bolted belay a step to the left, under a prominent narrow chimney.
belay.3: A tiny belay ledge above the small overhang and the jigsaw-like rock.
belay.4: Belay on the crest of the headwall, at the top of the long splitter crack.
